CompilationReportResponse.description:
Full compilation report with per-stage timings.

``status`` discriminates a clean compile from a degraded one. The job ROW
stays ``completed`` for both -- a video was produced and is billable -- so
this nested field is the only place a caller can learn that something the
user asked for was dropped. ``degradations`` names each dropped feature and
a fixed, sanitised reason.

``status`` is one of:

* ``success``        -- the producer recorded no drops from the sites it
  COVERS. It is not a guarantee that nothing was dropped: coverage is
  partial and enumerated in ``_finalize._finalize`` and
  ``tests/unit/test_degradation_coverage.py``.
* ``partial_success`` -- at least one COVERED feature was dropped
* ``unknown``        -- the report predates status derivation, so NOTHING can
  be concluded. This is NOT a synonym for success: defaulting absence to
  "success" would make the API assert a clean compile for a report that
  never carried the claim.

``subtitle_error`` is deliberately NOT surfaced. The producer writes it into
the report blob, but its "file not found" branch echoes a resolved server
path and its exception branch echoes up to 4000 chars of ffmpeg detail --
the path-existence oracle ``_apply_subtitles``' own docstring refuses to
return. The subtitle drop is reported through ``degradations`` instead,
with a fixed reason.
CompilationReportResponse.title: CompilationReportResponse

Only overlay-designed templates accept it (full-frame card templates paint their own opaque stage and are refused); inline 'html' owns its own backdrop and is always allowed. ScreenCaptureStep.description:
One step of a single-pass per-screen capture of a live SPA.

The capturer navigates the base URL once, then walks this ordered step
list. Per step it applies, in a fixed order: ``viewport`` (resize) →
``goto`` (full navigation to a different absolute URL) → ``click`` (advance
the SPA in-place) → ``scroll_to`` (bring a section on-screen) → ``wait_for``
(await a content selector) → ``settle_ms`` pause → ONE screenshot iff
``capture_id`` is set. Every modifier soft-fails independently (a missed
target is logged and skipped, like :class:`InteractionStep`), so a stale
selector never costs the screenshot. A step with no ``capture_id`` (e.g. a
persona switch that only reveals nav) advances without capturing — needed
because some nav is ``display:none`` until a prior click.

``selector`` / ``scroll_to`` / ``wait_for`` are Playwright selectors (CSS or
the ``text=`` engine, e.g. ``.nav-item >> text="Build"``); ``scroll_to`` also
accepts the literal ``"bottom"`` to scroll to the page foot. ``goto`` is for
multi-page shotlists — a full navigation, distinct from an in-SPA ``click``;
it is a no-op when it already equals the current URL. ``viewport`` overrides
the context-wide viewport for this step (and stays in effect until the next
``viewport`` step).

capture_id.description: Screen id; screenshot taken (and keyed by this) when set
capture_id.title: Capture Id

goto.description: Full navigation to this absolute http(s) URL before the shot (multi-page)
goto.title: Goto

scroll_to.description: Scroll a selector into view before the shot, or 'bottom' for the page foot
scroll_to.title: Scroll To

settle_ms.description: Pause after the action before the screenshot
settle_ms.title: Settle Ms

viewport.description: Per-step viewport override (else the context-wide viewport)
viewport.title: Viewport

wait_for.description: Await this selector before taking the screenshot
wait_for.title: Wait For

ScreenCaptureStep.title: ScreenCaptureStep

get.description:
Server-Sent Events stream for job status updates.

The ``{tenant_id}`` path parameter must equal the caller's own tenant.

Before this guard the parameter was passed straight into the Redis pub/sub
subscribe, so any authenticated caller naming another tenant's id received a
live feed of that tenant's job events. Redis has no RLS backstop, so nothing
downstream caught it.

On the path parameter, what is actually known: it is a published contract in
THIS repo — ``README.md``, the ``/api`` endpoint map in ``src/asgi.py`` and
the ``stream_production_events`` operation id all carry it. No consumer of
``/events/{tenant_id}`` was found anywhere in the w2v tree; the frontend's SSE
is ``/api/projects/{id}/events`` on the orchestrator, not this route. A
browser ``EventSource`` cannot set ``Authorization`` or ``X-Tenant-Id``
headers at all, so no browser client could ever have authenticated here. The
parameter is therefore kept only because removing a published path is a
separate API decision, not because a caller is known to depend on it. It is a
redundant echo of the caller's identity, validated on every request.

Super-admin "browse as tenant" does NOT survive this check over a Keycloak
JWT. ``_apply_effective_tenant`` (``w2v_common/auth/middleware.py:292``) is
invoked from exactly one site (``:758``), inside the license-token branch, and
only for subjects listed in ``AUTH_DELEGATING_SUBJECTS``. The Keycloak-JWT
branch (``:660-698``) sets ``request.state.tenant_id`` straight from the
``tenant_id`` claim (falling back to ``sub``) and never looks at
``X-Active-Tenant-Id``. Consequence: a super-admin browsing as tenant B over a
Keycloak JWT still carries their OWN tenant in ``request.state.tenant_id``,
so ``GET /events/<tenant-B>`` returns 403 for them. That is the intended
trade: this route has no admin-impersonation path, and the fix for an admin
who needs one is an explicit elevation check, not a looser comparison.

403, not 404: the tenant id is not a secret, the subscription simply is not
the caller's to open. Same rationale as ai_content_generation_service PR #91.

Args:
    tenant_id: Tenant whose events to subscribe to. Must be the caller's own.
    request: FastAPI request (used for disconnect detection and Redis access).

Returns:
    StreamingResponse with SSE-formatted event data.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 403 if the caller has no resolved tenant, or if
        ``tenant_id`` is not the caller's tenant.
Combined health check for all components.

Kubernetes liveness probe -- process alive AND recording executor moving.

Why LIVENESS and not readiness: the failure this exists to catch is a
WEDGED recording executor (slots held by a job that will never finish, so
every subsequent job sits in ``queued`` until the reaper fails it). Pulling
the pod out of the Service, which is all readiness does, would take the
HTTP API down too and leave the wedge in place -- nothing else picks the
work up. A restart is the actual remedy: it drops the leaked slots and the
executor resumes. So the signal belongs on the probe that restarts.

Why it cannot flap: :pymeth:`RecordingConcurrencyManager.stall_status`
reports healthy whenever the wait queue is empty, so an idle service -- for
any length of time -- stays alive. Only work that is demonstrably WAITING
while no slot is admitted or released for longer than
``executor_stall_threshold_seconds`` fails the probe.
